rows.citation: Sáray, S., Rössert, C. A., Appukuttan, S., et al. (2021). HippoUnit: A software tool for the automated testing and systematic comparison of detailed models of hippocampal neurons based on electrophysiological data. PLOS Computational Biology 17:e1008114.
rows.model_type: detailed multicompartmental rat hippocampal CA1 pyramidal cell (and interneuron) models in NEURON; validation against experimental data
rows.controlled_mutations: no - compares independently published and BluePyOpt-optimized models against experimental data; no seeded single-fault edits of a reference model.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - five tests: somatic current steps of several amplitudes, 1 s escalating steps for depolarization block, bAP, PSP attenuation, oblique synaptic integration.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - Somatic Features Test extracts eFEL spike-shape, timing, subthreshold and sag features; scores are deviations from experimental means.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - protocols are fixed to mirror the source experiments (configurable via JSON); no selection of a compact or cost-bounded battery.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - optimized models are validated on eFEL features beyond those used for fitting; no held-out model or fault-family split for a detection method.
rows.ai_transformations: no - no AI-assisted or automated code transformations are studied.
rows.software: HippoUnit https://github.com/KaliLab/hippounit (GitHub API license BSD-3-Clause; PyPI hippounit 1.4.1 declares MIT - conflict unresolved); demos https://github.com/KaliLab/HippoUnit_demo
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: HippoUnit scores models against experimental data (biological validity). NeuroSem would compare a model with its own edited versions, using refinement-calibrated tolerances, seeded single-fault mutants, greedy protocol selection and held-out models/mutation family. HippoUnit's SciUnit capability/test pattern and eFEL use are reusable precedent, not a novelty claim for NeuroSem.

rows.citation: Tomko, M., Benuskova, L., Jedlicka, P. (2021). A new reduced-morphology model for CA1 pyramidal cells and its validation and comparison with other models using HippoUnit. Scientific Reports 11:7615.
rows.model_type: reduced-morphology and full-morphology CA1 pyramidal cell models in NEURON
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - replaces the whole ion-channel set of three reduced models with the new model's channels (vTo21 variants) and retests; multi-change edits, not single recorded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - full HippoUnit battery: somatic steps from -1.0 to 1.0 nA, depolarization block, bAP, PSP attenuation and oblique integration tests.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - 73 eFEL somatic features plus depolarization-block and dendritic attenuation measures, summarized as error scores.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - uses the fixed HippoUnit battery; manual conductance tuning targets test scores, not protocol choice.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - the model was hand-tuned toward the same HippoUnit tests used to compare it; no held-out split.
rows.software: HippoUnit fork https://github.com/tomko-neuron/HippoUnit (URL cited in the paper's full text; repository not separately checked via API)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: An application study showing that a multi-test battery separates model variants by agreement with data. NeuroSem would instead measure divergence of edited models from their own reference with calibrated tolerances, single-fault mutants, protocol selection and held-out evaluation.
rows.verification_method: Crossref /works/10.1038/s41598-021-87002-7 (title, 3 authors, Scientific Reports, 2021-04-07, vol 11, 7615, abstract); Europe PMC (PMID 33828151, PMC8027802) fullTextXML methods and results sections

rows.citation: Birgiolas, J., Haynes, V., Gleeson, P., et al. (2023). NeuroML-DB: Sharing and characterizing data-driven neuroscience models described in NeuroML. PLOS Computational Biology 19:e1010941.
rows.model_type: database of 1,500+ NeuroML channel, cell and network models; cell models converted by jNeuroML to NEURON for simulation
rows.controlled_mutations: no - characterizes existing published models; correctness of NeuroML-to-NEURON conversion is attributed to the OSB Model Validation framework, not mutation testing.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - Allen Cell Types protocols (square, long square, pink noise, ramp, short square, short square triple) plus rheobase-multiple steps and ramps.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - 38 Druckmann-style properties implemented as NeuronUnit tests, plus resting spike count, ramp first-spike time and frequency filtering.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - discusses that fixed 1.5x/3x rheobase stimuli poorly characterize some model clusters and suggests better protocols; no algorithmic selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - database-scale PCA and nested clustering of model properties; no held-out detection evaluation.
rows.software: NeuroML-DB https://neuroml-db.org (HTTP 200 on 2026-09-13); code https://github.com/scrook/neuroml-db (GitHub API license MIT); property tests built on NeuronUnit https://github.com/scidash/neuronunit
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Closest NeuroML-specific precedent for multi-protocol, rheobase-normalized feature fingerprints of models. It fingerprints different models for search and clustering (and imputes missing properties with min/max/mean). NeuroSem would compare a reference with edited versions, keep undefined features undefined, calibrate tolerances by refinement, seed mutants, select a compact battery and evaluate on held-out models and a mutation family.

rows.citation: Podlaski, W. F., Seeholzer, A., Groschner, L. N., et al. (2017). Mapping the function of neuronal ion channels in model and experiment. eLife 6:e22152.
rows.model_type: 2,378 NEURON ion-channel models (Kv, Nav, Cav, KCa, Ih) simulated in a standard single-compartment voltage-clamp harness
rows.controlled_mutations: no - clusters existing published channel models and traces their genealogy; no seeded edits or fault injection.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - battery of voltage-clamp protocols including activation, inactivation, deactivation, ramp and action-potential waveform.
rows.electrophysiology_features: partial - current responses compressed by PCA into per-protocol score vectors; voltage-clamp currents, not current-clamp spiking features.
rows.protocol_optimization: partial - qualitatively assesses which protocols separate channel subtypes; no optimization or budgeted protocol selection.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - a new uncatalogued model and experimental recordings are placed into existing clusters; not a held-out detection evaluation.
rows.software: ICGenealogy web resource https://icg.neurotheory.ox.ac.uk (HTTP 200 on 2026-09-13); channel repositories e.g. https://github.com/icgenealogy/icg-channels-K (GitHub API license GPL-3.0); related https://github.com/OpenSourceBrain/IonChannelGenealogyShowcase (no license reported)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Behavioral fingerprinting at the ion-channel level for classification, showing same-label models can behave differently. NeuroSem works at the cell level under current clamp and targets edit-induced drift relative to a reference, with calibrated tolerances, seeded mutants and selected batteries.

rows.citation: Reva, M., Rössert, C., Arnaudon, A., et al. (2023). A universal workflow for creation, validation, and generalization of detailed neuronal models. Patterns 4:100855.
rows.model_type: detailed multicompartmental rat somatosensory cortex e-models (NEURON; workflow can export NeuroML) optimized with BluePyOpt
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - sensitivity analysis lowers each parameter by 10, 50 and 90% one at a time and measures e-feature changes; not a detection study.
rows.multiple_stimuli: yes - several somatic step protocols for optimization; Ramp, sAHP and IDHyperpol plus dendritic bAP and EPSP tests for validation.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - BluePyEfe e-features (spike count, AP amplitude, ISIs, sag ratio, AHP depth) at rheobase-normalized stimulus targets.
rows.protocol_optimization: no - model parameters are optimized; protocols are chosen by design, not selected algorithmically.
rows.heldout_evaluation: partial - validates on stimuli unused in fitting and generalizes e-models to many unseen morphologies; aim is fidelity, not change detection.
rows.software: SSCxEModelExamples https://github.com/BlueBrain/SSCxEModelExamples (cited in paper; GitHub license NOASSERTION); related pipeline BluePyEModel https://github.com/openbraininstitute/BluePyEModel (PyPI bluepyemodel 1.0.47, Apache-2.0 text; GitHub NOASSERTION; link to this paper not verified by me)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Builds and validates models against experimental data, including unseen-stimulus validation and one-at-a-time parameter perturbation. NeuroSem instead asks whether edits to an existing model silently change behavior, adding refinement-calibrated tolerances, admissible-mutant classification, greedy battery selection and a held-out mutation family. Its rheobase-relative stimuli are reusable practice.

rows.citation: Tennøe, S., Halnes, G., Einevoll, G. T. (2018). Uncertainpy: A Python Toolbox for Uncertainty Quantification and Sensitivity Analysis in Computational Neuroscience. Frontiers in Neuroinformatics 12:49.
rows.model_type: general neuroscience models: Hodgkin-Huxley point neuron, NEURON multicompartment thalamic interneuron, NEST recurrent network (plus a non-neural example)
rows.controlled_mutations: partial - parameters are sampled from distributions (e.g., uniform +/-10%) for uncertainty and sensitivity analysis; no discrete recorded faults.
rows.multiple_stimuli: no - case studies each use one fixed input (e.g., a single current injection); the toolbox does not organize stimulus batteries.
rows.electrophysiology_features: yes - built-in spiking features and the full eFEL feature set; network features via Elephant.
rows.heldout_evaluation: no - reports uncertainty and sensitivity estimates via polynomial chaos or quasi-Monte Carlo; no held-out evaluation.
rows.software: Uncertainpy https://github.com/simetenn/uncertainpy (GitHub API license GPL-3.0; PyPI uncertainpy 1.2.3, GNU GPLv3); docs http://uncertainpy.readthedocs.io/ (URL from paper)
rows.distinction_from_neurosem: Quantifies how continuous parameter uncertainty propagates to features under one input. NeuroSem asks whether discrete edits produce divergence beyond numerical tolerance across several stimuli, and selects batteries that expose it. Uncertainpy could support tolerance-sensitivity analysis but does not address mutants or battery selection.
